result.topic_en: A scholium tabulating the complete cycles of residues of powers of primitive roots for the primes 3 to 23, and remarking that no method is yet known for finding primitive roots for an arbitrary prime.
result.transcription:
PER NVMEROS PRIMOS. 101
Scholion.
39. Quo haec clarius intelligantur, conueniet
pro ſimplicioribus diuiſoribus primis tales ſeries re-
ſiduorum completas conſpectui exponi, vbi quidem
progreſſiones geometricas, vnde naſcuntur, non opus
eſt exponi, quia radix ſemper ſecundo termino ſe-
riei reſiduorum eſt aequalis; ſed ſufficiet generalem
progreſſionem in capite poſuiſſe, vt inde exponen-
tes, quibus ſinguli termini in ſeriebus reſiduorum
reſpondent, perſpiciantur:
$\begin{array}{c|l} & a^0, a^1, a^2, a^3, a^4, a^5, a^6, a^7, a^8, a^9, a^{10}, a^{11}, a^{12}, a^{13}, a^{14}, a^{15}, a^{16}, a^{17}, a^{18}, a^{19}, a^{20} \text{ etc.} \\ \hline 3 & 1, 2 | 1, 2 | 1, 2 | 1, 2 | 1, 2 | 1, 2 | 1, 2 | 1, 2 | 1, 2 | 1, 2 | 1, \text{ etc.} \\ 5 & 1, 2, 4, 3 | 1, 2, 4, 3 | 1, 2, 4, 3 | 1, 2, 4, 3 | 1, 2, 4, 3 | 1, 2 \text{ etc.} \\ 7 & 1, 3, 2, 6, 4, 5 | 1, 3, 2, 6, 4, 5 | 1, 3, 2, 6, 4, 5 | 1, 3, 2, 6 \text{ etc.} \\ 11 & 1, 2, 4, 8, 5, 10, 9, 7, 3, 6 | 1, 2, 4, 8, 5, 10, 9, 7, 3, 6 | 1, 2 \text{ etc.} \\ 13 & 1, 2, 4, 8, 3, 6, 12, 11, 9, 5, 10, 7 | 1, 2, 4, 8, 3, 6, 12, 11, 9, 5, \text{ etc.} \\ 17 & 1, 3, 9, 10, 13, 5, 15, 11, 16, 14, 8, 7, 4, 12, 2, 6 | 1, 3, 9, 10, 13, 5 \text{ etc.} \\ 19 & 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 13, 7, 14, 9, 18, 17, 15, 11, 3, 6, 12, 5, 10 | 1, 2, 4, 8 \text{ etc.} \\ 23 & 1, 5, 2, 10, 4, 20, 8, 17, 16, 11, 9, 22, 18, 21, 13, 19, 3, 15, 6, 7, 12, 14 | \text{ etc.} \end{array}$
(Diuiſor primus)
Radices igitur, quibus hic pro iſtis diuiſoribus pri-
mis ſumus vſi, ſunt primitiuae, quia earum poteſta-
tes omnia diuerſa reſidua diuiſore minora ſuppedi-
tant, quibus exhauſtis demum vnitas recurrit, et
ſeries eodem ordine vti ab initio progrediuntur.
Via quidem adhuc non patet, tales radices primiti-
uas pro quouis diuiſore primo inueniendi, neque
etiam demonſtratio, qua tales radices primitiuas ſem-
per dari euici, methodum eas inueniendi declarat.
N 3 Pro

items.quote: Via quidem adhuc non patet, tales radices primitiuas pro quouis diuiſore primo inueniendi
items.english: Indeed, no way is yet apparent of finding such primitive roots for any given prime divisor.

items.quote: neque etiam demonſtratio, qua tales radices primitiuas ſemper dari euici, methodum eas inueniendi declarat.
items.english: Nor does the demonstration by which I proved that such primitive roots always exist reveal a method of finding them.

items.quote: Radices igitur, quibus hic pro iſtis diuiſoribus primis ſumus vſi, ſunt primitiuae, quia earum poteſtates omnia diuerſa reſidua diuiſore minora ſuppeditant, quibus exhauſtis demum vnitas recurrit
items.english: The roots we have used here for these prime divisors are therefore primitive, because their powers supply all the different residues less than the divisor, and only once these are exhausted does unity recur.
